facts: Apr 2023: Reddit says it will charge for API access. On May 31, Apollo's developer reveals the price: $12,000 per 50 million calls, about $0.24 per 1,000.
TechCrunch
He estimates the fees at about $20 million a year.
TechCrunch
June 12, 2023: more than 8,000 subreddits go private or read-only in a 48-hour blackout. Some stay dark longer.
TechCrunch
July 2023: BotDefense's volunteers shut the anti-spam bot down, blaming the API changes and Reddit's treatment of moderators and developers. Their shutdown post put its ban list at 144,926 accounts.
BotDefense; Ars Technica
Feb 2024: Reddit licenses its data to Google for AI, reported at about $60 million a year.
Reuters
Mar 2024: Reddit goes public. It lets some users and moderators buy shares at the offering price.
CNBC
May 2024: Reddit announces a data partnership with OpenAI.
OpenAI
July 2024: Reddit's robots.txt shuts out crawlers. Google, which pays Reddit, stays the only major search engine with fresh Reddit results.
9to5Mac

pages.title: Since then
facts: June 2025: Reddit sues Anthropic, alleging it scraped Reddit without a license, kept accessing the site after saying it had stopped, and used posts users had deleted. Anthropic disputes the claims. In September 2026 a San Francisco judge lets the contract and unfair-competition claims proceed; there is no ruling on the merits.
TechCrunch; Bloomberg Law
Aug 2025: Reddit blocks the Wayback Machine from archiving most of the site, citing AI scraping.
Nieman Lab
Sept 30, 2026: Reddit says RSS feeds end Nov 13, 2026, and its free public API closes in March 2027.
PPC Land; Decrypt
Oct 29, 2026: Reddit says it will shift to a primarily logged-in experience, testing first outside the US.
TechCrunch
